title: Hidden Authentication Side-Effects (Temporal Coupling)
pattern: A method whose signature and name implies a side-effect-free query (e.g., checking a password) silently mutates system state (e.g., initializing a session).
why_bad: Violates Command-Query Separation. This creates a temporal coupling where the validation function can only be safely called at specific times, leading to security flaws (like accidentally clearing an existing session or failing to audit).
detection: A query-like method (returning boolean or validation proof) invoking state mutation functions internally.
fix: Refactor to separate queries from modifiers. Let verification methods remain pure and side-effect-free; perform session lifecycle mutations in separate explicit command actions.
source: `Robert C. Martin - Clean Code (2008)`, Ch 3, p. 44.
